chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Hammad from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'A man sells dirhams for dinars on credit (deferred payment).' He said, 'There is no objection (it is permissible).'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell gold for silver with deferred payment in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permits exchanging gold for silver with deferred payment (*nasi'ah*), challenging the stricter view that immediate exchange (*taqabud*) is an absolute condition for all gold-silver transactions. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between the prohibition of *riba al-fadl* (excess) and *riba al-nasi'ah* (deferment), allowing for flexibility in commercial contracts when the weight and measure are equal. It reflects the practical juristic approach of the Imams in facilitating trade while maintaining the core principles of fairness in currency exchange.
